title: The fruits of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23)
hook: the Latin Bible lists twelve: charity, joy, peace, patience and more (CCC 1832)

segments.voice: Yesterday, all one: neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, male nor female. Your line was all one in christ.

Open a modern Bible to Galatians chapter five and count the fruit of the Spirit. Nine. Now open the Douay-Rheims to the same verse and count again. Twelve. Nobody slipped in a few extra. The difference is centuries old, and it says something about how the Bible traveled. Paul has just listed what he calls the works of the flesh: enmities, contentions, envy, anger, quarrels, drunkenness and more. Now he lists the opposite, and the Catholic Church still counts it the old way.
screen: `NINE IN ONE BIBLE.` → `TWELVE IN ANOTHER.` → `THE WORKS OF THE FLESH, THEN THE FRUIT.`

segments.voice: Here it is in the Douay-Rheims: "But the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity." Twelve. The Greek text behind modern Bibles has nine. The old Latin Bible has twelve; some scholars think early translators rendered a few Greek words with two Latin ones. The Catechism lists the twelve, and says that the tradition of the Church counts them so. Look at two words Paul chose. First, works versus fruit. Works are things you make: you build them, you produce them. Fruit grows. You can water a tree and prune it, but you can't force an apple. Paul's point is that these qualities are what the Spirit grows in a life given over to God. Second, fruit, not fruits. In Paul's Greek it's singular, one fruit, the way one orange has many segments. Charity heads the list, and the others may be read as its flavors. Today's line comes from Jesus in Matthew's Gospel, talking about telling true teachers from false: "By their fruits you shall know them." A tree is known by what it bears. Catholics use the twelve as a kind of mirror. Not a checklist to grade yourself, but a way to notice what's already growing. And the list is very ordinary. Patience in traffic. Mildness on the phone. Joy at a kitchen table. Nothing on it requires a miracle, just a life where something is quietly growing.
screen: `TWELVE IN LATIN, NINE IN GREEK.` · `WORKS ARE MADE, FRUIT GROWS.` · `ONE FRUIT, MANY FLAVORS.` · `KNOWN BY WHAT IT BEARS.` · then, large: `BY THEIR FRUITS YOU SHALL KNOW THEM.`

segments.voice: Let the list pass slowly through your mind: charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long patience, mildness, faith, modesty, self-control, chastity. Don't grade yourself; just ask which one you've actually seen in yourself this week, even once, even small, and remember the scene. If you pray, thank God for what's growing; if not, notice it and be glad.
Karpos. The Greek word for fruit, singular: one fruit of the Spirit with many flavors, charity first among them. Today's word.
Your line: by their fruits. And that's week eighty-three: enigma, where is thy sting, earthen vessels, skolops, a cheerful giver, all one, and the fruits of the Spirit. Until tomorrow.
screen: `WEEK EIGHTY-THREE: GLASS · STING · CLAY · WEAKNESS · CHEERFUL · ONE · FRUITS`

chat.says: Why does my Catholic Bible list twelve fruits of the Spirit when my friend's lists nine?
options: The old Latin Bible lists twelve; the Greek text behind yours lists nine.
Catholics added three at a church council, to match the twelve apostles.
Paul wrote nine; the other three come from Jesus in Matthew's Gospel.
chat.meaning: The Greek text behind modern Bibles has nine; the old Latin has twelve. Some scholars think early translators rendered a few Greek words with two Latin ones.

Douay-Rheims.meaning: the old Catholic English translation of the Bible

Catechism.meaning: the Catholic Church's official summary of its teaching

longanimity.meaning: an old word for long patience

notes: Vulgate's twelve vs. the Greek nine: the extra three (longanimity, modesty, chastity) are usually explained as doublets in early Latin translation. Stated as 'probably'. Confirm.
CCC 1832 lists twelve 'according to the tradition of the Church'. Paraphrased. Confirm.
The practice's list uses modern equivalents (kindness, long patience, self-control) for benignity, longanimity, continency. Confirm acceptable.
